clue.text: Information store starts to defrag and thus degrade

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters

parts.note: first letters of defrag, and, thus
to abase is to degrade or humiliate

explanation.surface: An IT warning: running a defragmenter on your drive could corrupt the stored data.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pushes you to read 'defrag' as computer jargon; it just supplies its D.
explanation.definitionFit: An information store is a descriptive paraphrase: a database is where organised records are kept for retrieval.

clue.text: Simple Minds ultimately stops cycling old agreement

indicators.note: cycling means letters are rotated round from one end of the word to the other
stops means this letter closes off the other piece, coming at its end

parts.note: yea is an old word for yes, a vote of agreement

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Simple Minds, the Scottish band, finally quit touring and break an old deal.
explanation.walkthrough: Simple Minds is a Scottish rock band, which hides the definition. The S at the end of Minds 'stops' YEA, giving YEAS; 'cycling' moves the Y round to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Something easy is straightforward and needs no effort, which is what simple means here.

clue.text: Second adult to abandon Latin dance character overseas

indicators.note: the A leaves the word it was in

parts.note: A = adult; 'second' says which of the dance's three A's is dropped

explanation.surface: An adult drops out of a Latin dance class, leaving a partner stranded.
explanation.walkthrough: LAMBADA has three A's; removing the middle one gives the answer. 'Overseas' makes the character a foreign letter, here Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambda is a letter of the Greek alphabet, a character used abroad.

clue.text: Tense aquatic bird crushed by snake somewhere in South Africa

definitions.note: 'South Africa' here means the south of the continent, not the country

indicators.note: the snake squeezes round the other pieces, as a boa crushes prey

parts.note: a boa constrictor, whose letters wrap round the tense and the bird

explanation.surface: A nervous water bird being squeezed by a snake somewhere in the South African bush.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface places everything in South Africa the country; Botswana is its northern neighbour, in southern Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Botswana is a country in the south of the African continent.

clue.text: Breaking in, proposes tyranny

indicators.note: the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A burglar breaking in and then proposing tyranny.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma makes 'Breaking in' look like a phrase about burglary; the words split, with 'in' joining the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppression is cruel, unjust rule, which is tyranny.

clue.text: Gangster that is holding up police HQ?

parts.note: the Yard, short for Scotland Yard, London's Metropolitan Police headquarters

explanation.surface: A gangster holding up a police station, a bold raid on headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding up' looks like armed robbery; in a down entry it means placed beneath. A Yardie is a member of a Jamaican-origin criminal gang.
explanation.definitionFit: Yardie is British slang for a Jamaican gangster.

clue.text: Squid Game uncovered racial manoeuvring

indicators.note: manoeuvring means moving around, so these letters are shuffled into a new order
uncovered means the word loses its covers, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A nod to the TV drama Squid Game, its racial politics unmasked and argued over.
explanation.walkthrough: Squid Game is a Korean TV drama, so 'Squid' seems part of a title; it alone is the definition. 'Game uncovered' gives AM, which joins RACIAL to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Calamari is squid prepared as food, usually in battered rings, the Italian word for squid.

clue.text: Relations slain violently around west

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters sit on either side of this one
violently means roughly thrown about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: W is the compass abbreviation for west

explanation.surface: Relatives brutally murdered somewhere out in the west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slain violently' rearranges SLAIN to INLAS, and 'around' puts that round W for west.
explanation.definitionFit: In-laws are relatives by marriage, a family connection such as a mother-in-law or brother-in-law.

clue.text: Harpo dealt with new undesirable counterpart of widow?

indicators.note: the letters are dealt out afresh, like cards

parts.note: the setter's own pseudonym as fodder

explanation.surface: The setter Harpo sorting out some newly bereaved person, a widow's counterpart.
explanation.walkthrough: In typesetting, a widow and an orphan are both unwanted stray lines at the top or bottom of a column; the surface pushes towards bereavement instead.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing, an orphan is a lone line stranded from its paragraph, a typographic fault paired with the widow.

clue.text: Firm's fine when internally upset

indicators.note: internally upset means the inner letters are overturned, read the other way round, while the ends stay put

explanation.surface: A company is in good shape, though in-house there has been upheaval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' suggests a company but is an adjective for hard like oak. OKAY with its inside 'upset' turns KA around to AK.
explanation.definitionFit: Oaky means like oak, and oak is proverbially hard, so here oaky stands for hard and solid.

clue.text: Coping with much support, adults bear struggles

indicators.note: the letters wrestle into a new order

explanation.surface: Grown-ups cope with their struggles thanks to plenty of emotional support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coping' and 'support' look emotional; a coping is the top course of a wall, and a balustrade is a coping rail held up by many balusters.
explanation.definitionFit: A balustrade is a rail or coping resting on a row of supporting balusters.

clue.text: Trouble held back plant

indicators.note: the letters are read backwards

parts.note: had = held; the whole string AIL+HAD is then read backwards

explanation.surface: Some trouble held up delivery of a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held back' looks like one phrase meaning delayed; 'held' is HAD and 'back' reverses everything before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Plant is the broad class: the dahlia is a tuberous flowering plant named after the botanist Anders Dahl.

clue.text: Time taken for nearest neighbour to come round again?

definitions.meaning: the surface means the people next door; the setter means Earth's nearest neighbour in space
reads as a return visit; the setter means completing an orbit and a full cycle of phases

explanation.surface: How long before the people next door drop in again?
explanation.walkthrough: The neighbour sounds like the person next door; it is the Moon, Earth's nearest neighbour, and 'come round' is its orbit.
explanation.definitionFit: Time taken is a period, and this one is the roughly 29.5 days the Moon needs to complete one cycle of phases.

clue.text: Update me — he wants different wife?

indicators.note: the letters are made different by rearranging

explanation.surface: Bring me up to date: this man wants a different wife?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Different wife' looks like one idea; 'different' works on 'he wants' and 'wife' supplies only W.
explanation.definitionFit: "What's new?" is how you ask someone to update you.

clue.text: Ineffectual sort of check on unopened list of options around university

parts.note: a menu without its first letter, split to hold U: E(U)NU

explanation.surface: Someone who can only manage a feeble check of the menu round the college.
explanation.walkthrough: A eunuch is used figuratively for a man or body with no power, hence ineffectual.
explanation.definitionFit: A eunuch, figuratively, is a powerless, ineffectual person.

clue.text: Pet food not wrapped in something waxy

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the waxy thing

parts.note: a candle is made of wax

indicators.note: not wrapped means the outer letters, its wrapping, are removed

explanation.surface: Pet food served loose, not packaged, inside a waxy container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' looks like an animal but is a verb, to fondle. 'food not wrapped' leaves OO, which goes in CANDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To canoodle is to kiss and cuddle amorously, and to pet is to caress in the same way.

clue.text: Disappear à la goods vehicle?

parts.note: -ish = in the style of, like à la

explanation.surface: A question about disappearing the way a delivery van does.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads VANISH as 'van-ish', in the manner of a van, with 'à la' turned into the suffix ISH.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words mean to go out of sight.

clue.text: Shelter with presumably one or more layers under roof

definitions.text: Shelter with presumably one or more layers
definitions.meaning: reads as a building whose roof has layers of material
the setter means egg-laying birds living under the roof

explanation.surface: A description of a shelter with several layers of roofing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Layers' reads as strata of material; it means hens that lay eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelter is the broad class: this one is the hut where laying hens roost and nest.

clue.text: Former farewell involves lifting drink

indicators.note: involves means the farewell word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: bye is a word of farewell

indicators.note: lifting in a down clue means raising the word up, so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: nog is a drink, as in eggnog, or a strong ale

explanation.surface: A goodbye to the past that includes raising a glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifting' turns NOG upwards to GON in this down clue, and BYE 'involves' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bygone describes something from times past, so it is a synonym of former.

clue.text: Bombastic outburst breaks cautious guarantee

indicators.note: the outburst breaks into the other word

parts.note: a rant, which breaks into the cautious word

explanation.surface: A customer's furious outburst breaks a careful promise from the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaks' looks like breaking a promise; here it means breaking into WARY.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a warranty is a maker's written promise to repair or replace, a guarantee.

clue.text: Charm a beast, given time

parts.note: a mule, a beast of burden

explanation.surface: Given enough time, you can charm a wild animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charm' looks like a verb; it is the noun, a lucky trinket.
explanation.definitionFit: Charm as a noun is a lucky object, and an amulet is one worn to ward off harm.

clue.text: Fruit bar, 50% pineapple

indicators.note: half of the word is taken

parts.note: ananas, the word for pineapple in French and many other languages, cut in half

explanation.surface: A fruit snack bar that is half pineapple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruit bar' reads as a snack; the words split. Pineapple is 'ananas' across much of Europe, so half the word is ANA.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the banana is a tropical fruit, as the pineapple in the wordplay is too.

clue.text: Hamper opinion about demand

indicators.note: the opinion goes about the demand

parts.note: 'my bet is' = my opinion is; split: B…ET
an ask, a demand, which the opinion goes around

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone's views get in the way of a demand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamper' looks like the verb to hinder; it is the noun, a large basket with a lid.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamper as a noun is a large lidded basket, so the answer names the wider class it belongs to.

clue.text: Self-governing modus operandi in car intelligence

indicators.note: the method goes inside the intelligence

parts.note: nous = common sense, intelligence; split: NO…US
MO, abbreviation for modus operandi, inside: NO(MO)US

explanation.surface: A description of the operating method behind a self-driving car's artificial intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all about driverless cars, which are also called autonomous. Nous is British informal for practical good sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: autonomous is from Greek auto (self) plus nomos (law), a body making its own laws.

clue.text: Small piece of timber hit with heavy blows

parts.note: S = small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A small piece of wood being struck hard, as when splitting kindling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit with heavy blows' is the definition; slog is used in cricket for a hard, wild swing.
explanation.definitionFit: To slog is to hit hard and wildly, as in cricket or boxing.

clue.text: Setter and solvers upset church so much

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: setter and solvers together are US, reversed

explanation.surface: The setter and solvers have annoyed the church so much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reads as annoying the church; it only turns US over.
explanation.definitionFit: Such can mean so much, as in 'such fun'.

clue.text: Payment contributing to current allowance

indicators.note: the answer is made up from parts of the next words

explanation.surface: A payment added to someone's present allowance.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across two words; 'contributing to' says those words contribute letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Payment is the broad class: rental is money paid regularly for the use of property.

clue.text: Work out tax spanning years, off and on

indicators.note: spanning means the tax word stretches across and around the other letters

parts.note: excise is a tax on goods made at home

indicators.note: off and on means taking letters only every other time, skipping the rest

explanation.surface: Calculate a tax bill that covers several years, intermittently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work out' looks like doing a sum, but the answer is physical training. 'years, off and on' gives ER, and EXCISE is 'spanning' it.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise is to do physical training, which is exactly what to work out means in a gym.
